title: Publish per-model KV-cache performance profiles and enable profile-aware version pinning
creator: Marcos Silva
description:
Background: When we onboard new model variants (quantized/FP16/etc.) we currently run microbenchmarks but do not produce a standardized, discoverable KV-cache profile nor sequence-length distribution histograms that customers and the routing layer can consume. This ticket implements an end-to-end pipeline to produce, validate, and publish per-model KV-cache performance profiles and sequence-distribution metadata, and to wire those profiles into the model catalog for profile-aware version pinning and routing.

Goals:
- Run standardized long-context profiling (including KV hit/miss, KV retention/mmem pressure, and per-step latency) for each model variant and relevant sequence-length distributions (bins).
- Produce a compact, versioned profile artifact (kv_profile_v{N}) that includes: sequence-length histogram, kv-hit-rate by prefix length, tail/95/99 latency buckets for cold/warm cache, recommended kv_retention defaults, and kernel selection hints.
- Publish profiles to the model catalog (visible in the API and Console) with model_version + profile_version semantics (customers can pin to a model_version and a profile_version).
- Expose a server-side routing policy that falls back to compatible profile/model variants when a pinned profile is unavailable.

Technical approach and trade-offs:
- Profiling runner: Extend the existing benchmarking harness to run long-context workloads with replayable prompt sets and synthetic sequence distributions. Use a distributed runner to exercise different batch sizes and prefix warmup strategies. Trade-off: higher fidelity (per-token traces) vs storage costs — we will persist compressed histograms rather than full traces.
- Profile schema: Keep the profile as a flat metadata record (no nested JSON in storage PLANS) with keys for kv_profile_version, seq_bins (CSV of bin upper bounds), seq_counts (CSV), kv_hit_rates (CSV), latency_p95_warm/cold, latency_p99_warm/cold, recommended_retention_ms, kernel_hint. This keeps the catalog queriable and small.
- Publishing pipeline: Two-stage: (1) profiler-run produces artifacts in s3://redwood-model-profiles/{model}/{model_version}/kv_profile_v{N}.json.gz and summary metadata in our catalog DB; (2) publisher validates artifact checksums and marks profile as "verified" after a quick regression check against golden prompts.
- Version pinning: Extend model catalog API to accept profile_version when creating deployments. Deployment DSL semantics: pinned_model=(model@model_version)+profile=(kv_profile_vN). If profile missing, routing uses fallback policy described in acceptance criteria.
- Performance concern: Running full long-context profiles for every push is expensive. We will: (a) run lightweight quick-profiles on PRs, (b) run full profiles on release gates or when model changes materially (checkpoint size, layer changes), and (c) cache profiles keyed by model fingerprint to avoid duplicate work.

Acceptance criteria:
- A profiler run exists that generates kv_profile_vN artifacts and seq-histogram summaries for a sample model (we will run on rwd-gpt-large/fp16 and rwd-gpt-large/int4).
- The published profile appears in the model catalog UI and API with the fields documented above.
- Users can create a deployment that pins both model_version and kv_profile_version; the API validates compatibility.
- Fallback routing: when a pinned profile_version is not available in a region, requests automatically fallback to: (1) same model_version + latest_verified_profile, (2) compatible model_variant + compatible_profile, (3) hosted default. Fallthrough must be logged and surfaced in Console.
- Integration tests and a canary job validate that profile-aware routing does not regress latency beyond a 5% SLA threshold on our sample workloads.

Acceptance test data and benchmarks (initial):
- Sample run: rwd-gpt-large/fp16, batch=8, sequences {512:50%, 1024:30%, 2048:20%} => kv_hit_rate(prefix<=128)=0.72, latency_p95_warm=82ms, latency_p99_warm=120ms, recommended_retention_ms=15000. Full trace saved compressed to s3 link.

Observability and docs:
- Console: Show profile list under model details with badge for verified and timestamp. Expose per-bin latency and hit-rate graphs.
- API: GET /models/{id}/profiles returns CSV-friendly fields and download URL.
- Docs: Confluence design doc (link below) plus a short quickstart for customers to pin profiles.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Storage and compute costs for profiling runs will grow with model count. Mitigation: sample profiles for major model families, deduplicate by model fingerprint, and TTL older profiles.
- Risk: Incorrect profile compatibility mapping could route incompatible profiles to a deployment and cause errors. Mitigation: strict compatibility checks in publisher and automated smoke-tests.

Related links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Per-Model+KV+Profile+Design
- Profiling runner PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3298
- Publisher service PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pull/462
acceptance_criteria: Profiler runner produces a kv_profile artifact and summary for at least two model variants (fp16 and int4)
Profiles are versioned and discoverable in model catalog API and Console
Deployment creation validates pinned profile compatibility and supports pinning to profile_version
Fallback routing is implemented and logged when pinned profile unavailable
Integration canary proves no >5% latency regression on sample workloads
comments: 2026-02-12 Marcos Silva: Initial ticket created. Blocker: need consensus on profile schema and storage path. Assigned to Priya.

2026-02-18 Priya Kapoor: Spike completed. Profiling harness extended to capture prefix-level KV hit rates and to emit compressed CSV summaries. PoC uploaded to s3://redwood-model-profiles/tmp/poctest.zip.

2026-02-23 Alex Chen: Reviewed spike; asked to add kernel_hint and recommended_retention fields to schema. Raised concern about per-bin resolution increasing storage 4x — decided on configurable binning with default 8 bins.
2026-03-02 Priya Kapoor: Publisher service skeleton implemented (catalog PR 462). Validation checks in place for checksum and model fingerprint match. Integration tests added in runtime PR 3298.

2026-03-08 QA: Canary run results attached: rwd-gpt-large/fp16 had p95 warm latency 82ms (baseline 80ms), within 3% — acceptable. Identified flaky test in long-context harness (timing dependent) — created ENG-11478 to follow up.
2026-03-10 Marcos Silva: Roadmap sync note — schedule full-profiles for new model family releases only. Add migration plan for existing catalog entries (backfill tooling).
